title: Who should govern artificial intelligence?
summary: The General Assembly debates how the world should govern AI: an expert panel, a global agency, binding rules, sharing skills with developing countries, and protections for voters, creators and children.

preambular.text: Reaffirming the Charter of the United Nations and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights,
Recalling the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and its seventeen Sustainable Development Goals,
Recalling also General Assembly resolution 78/265 on safe, secure and trustworthy artificial intelligence and resolution 78/311 on building artificial intelligence skills in developing countries,
Noting the Global Digital Compact, which the General Assembly adopted in 2024 as part of the Pact for the Future,
Noting that this draft deals only with civilian uses of artificial intelligence and not with weapons,

operative.text: Decides to set up an independent scientific panel of 40 experts from all regions, chosen through an open call by the Secretary-General, to report each year on what artificial intelligence can do and what risks it brings;
Requests the Secretary-General to propose a new United Nations agency for artificial intelligence, able to inspect and approve the most powerful AI systems;
Calls upon all States to agree a treaty that makes rules for the most dangerous AI systems legally binding, instead of relying on voluntary principles;
Urges richer countries to share computing power, training and technology with developing countries, on terms that both sides agree;
Encourages companies to label images, audio and video made by AI, so that voters can tell real material from fake, especially during elections;
Calls upon States to stop using AI systems that cannot be used without breaking human rights law;
Encourages safeguards for copyright and for personal data when AI systems are trained on books, art and online posts;
Urges States to require stronger protection for children who use AI tools, including age checks and the removal of harmful content.
